problem.problem:
Anne is quiet. Bob is not rough. Gary is big. Gary is kind. Gary is rough. Gary is young. Harry is young. All big people are furry. Young people are furry. All quiet, kind people are furry. If Harry is furry and Harry is quiet then Harry is round. Rough, kind people are quiet. Young, rough people are kind. All quiet, furry people are round. Furry people are rough.

Determine whether the following statement is true, false, or unknown:
Harry is not furry.
raw_logic_programs:
Predicates:
Quiet($x, bool) ::: Is x quiet?
Rough($x, bool) ::: Is x rough?
Big($x, bool) ::: Is x big?
Kind($x, bool) ::: Is x kind?
Young($x, bool) ::: Is x young?
Furry($x, bool) ::: Is x furry?
Round($x, bool) ::: Is x round?

Facts:
Quiet(Anne, True) ::: Anne is quiet.
Rough(Bob, False) ::: Bob is not rough.
Big(Gary, True) ::: Gary is big.
Kind(Gary, True) ::: Gary is kind.
Rough(Gary, True) ::: Gary is rough.
Young(Gary, True) ::: Gary is young.
Young(Harry, True) ::: Harry is young.

Rules:
Big($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: All big people are furry.
Young($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: Young people are furry.
Quiet($x, True) && Kind($x, True) >>> Furry($x, True) ::: All quiet, kind people are furry.
Furry(Harry, True) && Quiet(Harry, True) >>> Round(Harry, True) ::: If Harry is furry and Harry is quiet then Harry is round.
Rough($x, True) && Kind($x, True) >>> Quiet($x, True) ::: Rough, kind people are quiet.
Young($x, True) && Rough($x, True) >>> Kind($x, True) ::: Young, rough people are kind.
Quiet($x, True) && Furry($x, True) >>> Round($x, True) ::: All quiet, furry people are round.
Furry($x, True) >>> Rough($x, True) ::: Furry people are rough.

Query:
Furry(Harry, False) ::: Harry is not furry.
